segments.speaker: PA Senators Fetterman and McCormick join the Besties
segments.text: Now a look at the state of Pennsylvania.
segments.translation: 现在来看看宾夕法尼亚州的情况。

segments.speaker: PA Senators Fetterman and McCormick join the Besties
segments.text: It's one of the most important states in this presidential race.
segments.translation: 它是这次总统竞选中最重要的州之一。

segments.speaker: PA Senators Fetterman and McCormick join the Besties
segments.text: Both the Pennsylvania senators, Democrat John Fetterman and Republican Dave McCormack, voted in favor of the bill.
segments.translation: 宾夕法尼亚州的两名参议员，民主党人约翰·费特曼和共和党人戴夫·麦考马克，都投票赞成这项法案。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: In this situation, we both agreed that shutting our government down is wrong for our Commonwealth and for a nation.
segments.translation: 在这种情况下，我们都同意关闭政府对我们的联邦和国家都是错误的。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: So we're looking for ways to find common ground and when we disagree, we if we disagree, but when we can agree, we agree.
segments.translation: 所以我们正在寻找共同点，当我们意见不合时，如果我们意见不合，但当我们能达成一致时，我们就会达成一致。

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Our votes are about country over party at this point.
segments.translation: 在这一点上，我们的投票是国家利益高于党派利益。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Well, we're trying to set a good example because we have lots of disagreements, but we trust each other, we like one another, and we look for ways to work together.
segments.translation: 我们正在努力树立一个好榜样，因为我们有很多分歧，但我们彼此信任，彼此喜欢，并且寻找合作的方式。

segments.speaker: Bipartisanship in 2026, rejecting extremism
segments.text: I thought the best way to kick this off was to actually give both of you a few moments to just say what's on your mind.
segments.translation: 我认为最好的开场方式是给你们两位一些时间，说说你们心里想什么。

segments.speaker: Bipartisanship in 2026, rejecting extremism
segments.text: And so I think in the rules of parliamentary decorum, Senator Fennerdrum, as a senior sitting senator from Pennsylvania, maybe you can start.
segments.translation: 所以我想，根据议事礼仪规则，费特曼参议员，作为宾夕法尼亚州资深在任参议员，也许您可以先开始。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: I'm proud to call Senator McCormick a good friend.
segments.translation: 我很荣幸称麦考马克参议员为好朋友。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: And now things are very more polarized.
segments.translation: 现在事情变得更加两极分化了。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: And now I refuse to engage in the kinds of extremism.
segments.translation: 现在我拒绝参与那种极端主义。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: And you know, we're going to fight together for Pennsylvania and for a nation right now.
segments.translation: 你知道，我们现在将为宾夕法尼亚州和我们的国家共同奋斗。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: And we're going to continue to have conversations like this, you know, whether in Pennsylvania or here across.
segments.translation: 我们将继续进行这样的对话，你知道，无论是在宾夕法尼亚州还是在这里。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: So we we have to find a better way forward through a lot of the circumstances.
segments.translation: 所以我们必须在许多情况下找到更好的前进道路。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Yeah, Dave.
segments.translation: 是的，戴夫。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Yeah, I think, I mean, one of the the the benefits of being in a place like Pennsylvania is that the the voters expect us really to find ways to work together.
segments.translation: 是的，我认为，我的意思是，在宾夕法尼亚州这样的地方，好处之一是选民确实期望我们找到合作的方式。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And if you put this moment in perspective, I think it's probably the most consequential moment in all of our lifetimes.
segments.translation: 如果你把这个时刻放在一个宏观的角度来看，我认为这可能是我们一生中最具决定性的时刻。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And in fact, I think it might be the most consequential moment in humankind, which is, which is a big statement.
segments.translation: 事实上，我认为这可能是人类历史上最具决定性的时刻，这是一个很大的说法。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: So much change is happening.
segments.translation: 正在发生如此多的变化。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: It's artificial intelligence, of course, but it's, it's really how that's affecting everything.
segments.translation: 当然是人工智能，但它真正影响着一切。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Life sciences, defence energy, It's, it's a moment of enormous change.
segments.translation: 生命科学、国防能源，这是一个巨大变化的时刻。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And that that change creates a lot of anxiety that lends itself to polarization and extremes.
segments.translation: 而这种变化带来了很多焦虑，导致了两极分化和极端主义。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And so if there was ever a time where it's more important to find ways to work together, it it's now.
segments.translation: 所以，如果说有什么时候比现在更需要找到合作方式的话，那就是现在。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And so we've found ways to work together on everything from energy policy to fentanyl, the fentanyl crisis to anti-Semitism in Pennsylvania and across the country to drone technology.
segments.translation: 因此，我们找到了在从能源政策到芬太尼危机，从宾夕法尼亚州和全国的反犹太主义到无人机技术等所有问题上合作的方式。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And, and these are issues that are of such consequence that you can't get there by just being with your team.
segments.translation: 这些问题如此重要，你不能只靠自己的团队来解决。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: You have to be able to find common ground.
segments.translation: 你必须能够找到共同点。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And we've, we've really look for ways to do that.
segments.translation: 我们确实一直在寻找这样做的方法。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Yeah, I, I think he could confirm.
segments.translation: 是的，我想他可以证实。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Pennsylvania keeps you honest now.
segments.translation: 宾夕法尼亚州让你保持诚实。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: And now I'd like to remind everybody that we are the only two people in our respective cycles that flipped seats.
segments.translation: 现在我想提醒大家，我们是各自周期中唯一两位翻转了席位的人。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: You know, that's really, you know, both parties want that they, we, we want to flip seats.
segments.translation: 你知道，这确实是，你知道，两党都希望如此，我们都希望翻转席位。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: It's like, well, you know, we we've done that because I think we've rejected the extreme kinds of views and now it's better to work together for, for Pennsylvania or for our country for right now.
segments.translation: 就像，嗯，你知道，我们已经做到了，因为我认为我们拒绝了极端的观点，现在最好为宾夕法尼亚州或我们的国家共同努力。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: And AI is really, really important.
segments.translation: 人工智能真的非常非常重要。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: And and it will sometimes will put me at odds where the direction that the Democratic Party seems to be moving in that now.
segments.translation: 有时这会让我与民主党现在似乎正在发展的方向产生分歧。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: So now a moratorium for data Centers for me, that's a China first kinds of policy for that.
segments.translation: 所以现在，对我来说，数据中心的暂停令是一种“中国优先”的政策。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: I'm going to continue to push back that.
segments.translation: 我将继续反对这一点。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: I'm not going to describe that as a scourge.
segments.translation: 我不会将其描述为祸害。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: I'm going to describe that that is an incredible new opportunity.
segments.translation: 我将将其描述为一个令人难以置信的新机遇。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: And now you know, my friend, he, he organized an incredible symposium in Western Pennsylvania that brought AI together in energy.
segments.translation: 现在你知道，我的朋友，他在宾夕法尼亚州西部组织了一场精彩的研讨会，将人工智能与能源结合起来。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: And that's two parts of things Pennsylvania really brings to that table in this very, very important conversation.
segments.translation: 而这正是宾夕法尼亚州在这场非常重要的对话中能贡献的两部分内容。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: I think that we're at this point now where is it fair to say as goes Pennsylvania, as goes the rest of the country in the sense that if if you can find common ground in the state on these very thorny issues, maybe the rest of the country can find ground.
segments.translation: 我认为我们现在到了这样一个地步，公平地说，宾夕法尼亚州的情况如何，全国其他地方的情况也如何，意思是，如果你们能在州内这些棘手的问题上找到共同点，也许全国其他地方也能找到共同点。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: And the vice versa is also true.
segments.translation: 反之亦然。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: If you guys can't find resolution, what are the odds of California and West Virginia making it up find resolution.
segments.translation: 如果你们无法找到解决方案，加利福尼亚州和西弗吉尼亚州找到解决方案的可能性有多大？

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: So what is it like a day in the life in the US Senate trying to find these compromises?
segments.translation: 那么，在美国参议院，寻找这些妥协方案的日常生活是怎样的？

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Because from our perspective outside in, a lot of the time it just seems like nothing is happening.
segments.translation: 因为从我们外部人的角度来看，很多时候似乎什么都没有发生。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Dave.
segments.translation: 戴夫。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Yeah, I think if you step back, you, you would we, we, I know we look very similar, but we, we have, we have many somewhere back.
segments.translation: 是的，我想如果你退一步看，你会发现我们看起来很相似，但我们有很多相似之处。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: We do, we have, what's the difference?
segments.translation: 我们确实有，有什么不同？

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: We have similar backgrounds in the sense we both grew up in rural Pennsylvania and had similar, you know, similar childhoods.
segments.translation: 我们有相似的背景，我们都在宾夕法尼亚州的农村长大，有着相似的童年。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And John went into public service.
segments.translation: 约翰进入了公共服务领域。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: I, I left, went to West Point, went to the military, but we both came back from those those rural backgrounds.
segments.translation: 我离开了，去了西点军校，参了军，但我们都从那些农村背景回到了这里。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: But what's interesting in Pennsylvania is 19 electoral votes and that it's a microcosm of the country.
segments.translation: 但宾夕法尼亚州有趣的是它有19张选举人票，它是这个国家的一个缩影。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: You have these two big urban centers, Philadelphia and Pittsburgh, which are mostly Democrats.
segments.translation: 你有两个大的城市中心，费城和匹兹堡，它们主要是民主党人。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: You have these these rural areas that are mostly red, mostly Republican.
segments.translation: 你有这些主要是红色的农村地区，主要是共和党人。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And you got to build a coalition across those to win.
segments.translation: 你必须在这些地区建立一个联盟才能获胜。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: So ironically, a lot of the same people that voted for Senator Fetterman voted for me and, and, and voted for President Trump.
segments.translation: 所以讽刺的是，很多投票给费特曼参议员的人也投票给了我，也投票给了特朗普总统。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And, and that's the coalition you have to build.
segments.translation: 这就是你必须建立的联盟。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And in particular, it is a working families coalition.
segments.translation: 特别是，这是一个工薪家庭联盟。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: So the thing that's ironic is that even though all the, all the national unions would have vote would have endorsed Kamala Harris and Bob Casey, my opponent, the rank and file, 2/3 of the rank and file, the electricians, the pipe fitters, the steam fitters voted for me.
segments.translation: 所以讽刺的是，尽管所有全国性工会都会支持卡马拉·哈里斯和我的对手鲍勃·凯西，但普通会员中，三分之二的电工、管道工、蒸汽管道工都投票给了我。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Same with him.
segments.translation: 他也是一样。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: They voted for him.
segments.translation: 他们投票给了他。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: So it we actually, even though we have a lot of differences in our parties, we have come together around that coalition and that coalition includes a very significant Latino turn out, very significant African American turn out, the highest African American turn out in 2024 in the last 30 years.
segments.translation: 所以我们实际上，尽管我们的党派有很多分歧，但我们围绕着这个联盟走到了一起，这个联盟包括了非常重要的拉丁裔投票率，非常重要的非裔美国人投票率，是2024年过去30年中最高的非裔美国人投票率。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And so that coalition I think is up for grabs.
segments.translation: 所以这个联盟我认为是待定的。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Who wins that coalition in Pennsylvania and who wins it in the country, I think will dictate the future to a large degree in 2028 and beyond.
segments.translation: 谁赢得了宾夕法尼亚州的这个联盟，谁赢得了全国的这个联盟，我认为将在很大程度上决定2028年及以后的未来。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And so that's what we're working on together because we're trying to build that coalition to do good things together in Pennsylvania.
segments.translation: 所以这就是我们正在共同努力的，因为我们正在努力建立这个联盟，以便在宾夕法尼亚州共同做好事。

segments.speaker: All-time unpopularity in the Senate, the filibuster question, tribalism
segments.text: The Senate is at an all time low in terms of approval rating.
segments.translation: 参议院的支持率处于历史最低点。

segments.speaker: All-time unpopularity in the Senate, the filibuster question, tribalism
segments.text: We have the lowest approval rating of a president in history after Biden who was extremely low rated.
segments.translation: 在拜登之后，我们总统的支持率是历史上最低的，拜登的支持率已经非常低了。

segments.speaker: All-time unpopularity in the Senate, the filibuster question, tribalism
segments.text: You guys can't control the debt.
segments.translation: 你们无法控制债务。

segments.speaker: All-time unpopularity in the Senate, the filibuster question, tribalism
segments.text: The American populace believe we'd be in a golden age right now.
segments.translation: 美国民众相信我们现在应该处于黄金时代。

segments.speaker: All-time unpopularity in the Senate, the filibuster question, tribalism
segments.text: They're not seeing it.
segments.translation: 他们没有看到。

segments.speaker: All-time unpopularity in the Senate, the filibuster question, tribalism
segments.text: Inflation is soaring.
segments.translation: 通货膨胀飙升。

segments.speaker: All-time unpopularity in the Senate, the filibuster question, tribalism
segments.text: The president seems to be running amok, has no check in the house, and you guys are responsible.
segments.translation: 总统似乎在胡作非为，众议院对他没有任何制约，而你们负有责任。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Tell us what you really think.
segments.translation: 告诉我们你们真实的想法。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Other than this, Other than that, Misses Lincoln.
segments.translation: 除了这个，除了那个，林肯夫人。

segments.speaker: Speaker 5
segments.text: Well, and $40 trillion in debt and you're spending more than ever.
segments.translation: 嗯，还有40万亿美元的债务，你们花的钱比以往任何时候都多。

segments.speaker: Speaker 5
segments.text: So the American people, I think, are extremely frustrated with both parties.
segments.translation: 所以美国人民，我认为，对两党都非常沮丧。

segments.speaker: Speaker 5
segments.text: It's great to see you guys come together, but what are you going to do to bring back some balance between the branches of the government?
segments.translation: 很高兴看到你们走到一起，但你们将如何做才能使政府各部门之间恢复一些平衡？

segments.speaker: Speaker 5
segments.text: Because this does not seem to be going in the right direction for anybody but the people in this room, which is to say the top 10% of our society.
segments.translation: 因为这似乎对除了这个房间里的人，也就是我们社会中前10%的人之外的任何人来说，都不是一个正确的方向。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Well, I mean, for me, if you, you referenced inflation is soaring, well, just just recently, that's primarily driven by energy prices right now.
segments.translation: 嗯，我的意思是，对我来说，如果你提到通货膨胀飙升，那主要是由现在的能源价格驱动的。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Now why are those energy prices high?
segments.translation: 那么为什么这些能源价格很高呢？

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Well, because the president decided to hold Iran accountable and now I'm the only Democrat that actually agrees with that.
segments.translation: 嗯，因为总统决定追究伊朗的责任，现在我是唯一一个真正同意这一点的民主党人。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: That was not that was not a radical idea for a Democrats.
segments.translation: 这对于民主党人来说并不是一个激进的想法。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Every single person running for president as a Democrat said we must never allow Iran to acquire a nuclear bomb.
segments.translation: 每一个竞选总统的民主党人都说我们绝不能允许伊朗获得核弹。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: And now we have the opportunity to hold them accountable.
segments.translation: 现在我们有机会追究他们的责任。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Why?
segments.translation: 为什么？

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: That's why I continue to vote and against these war powers now too.
segments.translation: 这就是为什么我继续投票反对这些战争权力。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: So for inflation, yes, Now absolutely no one thinks of $5 a gallon is great.
segments.translation: 所以对于通货膨胀，是的，现在绝对没有人认为每加仑5美元是好事。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: But if you allow Iran to become nuclear, you know, that's going to seem quaint, you know, if $5 a gallon holding it too.
segments.translation: 但如果你允许伊朗拥有核武器，你知道，每加仑5美元就会显得微不足道了。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: So what's driving this economic conversation overall right now?
segments.translation: 那么现在推动这场经济对话的整体因素是什么呢？

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: So for me, I think what's most important now, turn everything as a part partisan thing.
segments.translation: 所以对我来说，我认为现在最重要的是把一切都变成党派之争。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: And that's the danger where if we despise Trump more than we are concerned about Iran becoming a nuclear power, that will have profound implications for not just in that region, but I'll ask for in a global stage for right now.
segments.translation: 这就是危险所在，如果我们憎恨特朗普胜过我们对伊朗成为核大国的担忧，那将不仅对该地区，而且对全球舞台产生深远影响。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: That's the difficulty moving forward.
segments.translation: 这就是前进的困难。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Now I've said this in the podcast, you know, if we're all in I, you know, who's the leaders party, I'm like, that's TDSA 100%.
segments.translation: 我在播客里说过，你知道，如果我们都投入其中，你知道，谁是领导人的党派，我就会说，那是100%的TDSA。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: You know, our party is defined by the opposition of whatever he comes out for.
segments.translation: 你知道，我们的党派是由反对他提出的任何东西来定义的。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: I've said he, Trump comes out for ice cream and lazy sundaes.
segments.translation: 我说过，特朗普提出冰淇淋和懒人圣代。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: We're we, we're going to hate that, you know, and we're going to vote it down.
segments.translation: 我们会讨厌它，你知道，我们会投票否决它。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Now we all have, we all have a bandwidth and we all have a platform.
segments.translation: 现在我们都有带宽，我们都有平台。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: You know, I feel like you have to discriminate.
segments.translation: 你知道，我觉得你必须有所区别。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: I don't care about the ballroom.
segments.translation: 我不在乎舞厅。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: If you want to build it, sure, great.
segments.translation: 如果你想建造它，当然，太好了。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: I was there for the the White House correspondent dinner and I saw how dangerous that was for for our leadership.

segments.text: I mean, like you're, you guys are going to be forced to confront the filibuster, which is this critical bulwark that sort of leaves some sort of attempt at finding common ground out there, But there's a lot of pressure to end it.
segments.translation: 我的意思是，你们将被迫面对阻挠议事，这是一个关键的堡垒，它在某种程度上为寻找共同点留下了空间，但现在结束它的压力很大。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: I think Senator Fenderman, you said you'd be supportive of ending the filibuster.
segments.translation: 我想费德曼参议员，你说过你会支持结束阻挠议事。

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Is that where we're going to just total tribalism?
segments.translation: 我们是不是要走向彻底的部落主义？

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Yeah, let's talk about the filibuster.
segments.translation: 是的，我们来谈谈阻挠议事。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Let's talk about that.
segments.translation: 我们来谈谈那个。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: The entire Democratic Party, including myself, we were so wrong about the filibuster in my cycle in 2020, every single Democrat identified.
segments.translation: 整个民主党，包括我自己，在2020年的周期中，我们对阻挠议事都大错特错了，每一个民主党人都认为。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: We have to, we have to eliminate the filibuster.
segments.translation: 我们必须，我们必须废除阻挠议事。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Seems like it makes sense now.
segments.translation: 现在看来这很有道理。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: And thank God, thank God we had people that stood there, whether it's Senator Manchin or Senator Cinema, you know, history has vindicated their wisdom to do that thing.
segments.translation: 感谢上帝，感谢上帝，我们有像曼钦参议员或西内马参议员这样坚持立场的人，历史已经证明了他们的智慧。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: And now Democrats, we all wanted to get rid of it in 22 and 2025.
segments.translation: 现在民主党人，我们都想在22年和2025年废除它。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: We love it.
segments.translation: 我们喜欢它。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: And now it now it forces people to work together with both sides.
segments.translation: 现在它迫使两边的人一起工作。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Now, if you turn the Senate into a smaller version of the House and majority majority now that would have profound, profound implications for now.
segments.translation: 现在，如果你把参议院变成众议院的一个缩小版，多数党说了算，那将对现在产生深远的影响。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: So how someone that be the first person to announce, hey, I was so wrong about that.
segments.translation: 所以，我将是第一个宣布，嘿，我当时大错特错了。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: That's one of the kinds of hill I would die on now to defend the filibuster, how important it is to the Senate, but also set it for the minority rights, whoever that happens to be in that time.
segments.translation: 现在，我将誓死捍卫阻挠议事，它对参议院的重要性，以及它对少数党权利的重要性，无论当时是哪个少数党。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: You know, that's what's so critical, what the filibuster is to governance here.
segments.translation: 你知道，这就是阻挠议事对这里的治理如此关键的原因。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: I would say first of all, Congress, but lots of institutions right now have very low public approval, very low trust that that's a huge problem.
segments.translation: 我想说，首先，国会，但现在很多机构的公众支持率都很低，信任度也很低，这是一个巨大的问题。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: It's across, it's across all areas, church, public officials, business in many cases.
segments.translation: 它遍及所有领域，教会、公职人员，在很多情况下还有企业。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: So we've got to rebuild trust in our institutions.
segments.translation: 所以我们必须重建对我们机构的信任。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And one of the ways you do that is to your own personal conduct.
segments.translation: 而做到这一点的方法之一就是你的个人行为。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: So one of the things we can do is try to set the example.
segments.translation: 所以我们能做的一件事就是努力树立榜样。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: If you look at my voting and his voting, I, I, I'm an unapologetic conservative.
segments.translation: 如果你看看我的投票和他的投票，我是一个毫不掩饰的保守派。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: I vote as a conservative.
segments.translation: 我投票时是保守派。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: At the same time, that doesn't mean you can't work together.
segments.translation: 同时，这并不意味着你们不能一起工作。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: So we look for every opportunity for bipartisan legislation.
segments.translation: 所以我们寻找一切机会进行两党立法。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: So I've got more bipartisan legislation than anybody.
segments.translation: 所以我比任何人都拥有更多的两党立法。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: We've collaborated on dozens of things together because you can do both.
segments.translation: 我们合作了几十件事，因为你可以两者兼顾。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And the filibuster, I mean, it is frustrating as a business person.
segments.translation: 而阻挠议事，我的意思是，作为一个商人，它令人沮丧。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: I was in business for 25 years, so frustrating.
segments.translation: 我经商25年，太令人沮丧了。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: The weight, the pace of of how slowly things move.
segments.translation: 事情进展缓慢的程度和速度。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: But I do think it creates the requirement, the impetus to get things done.
segments.translation: 但我确实认为它创造了完成事情的要求和动力。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And I would disagree with you.
segments.translation: 我不同意你的看法。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: I think a lot of big things have been done.
segments.translation: 我认为很多大事都已完成。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: I think if you look at the energy agenda, we can't win the AI race without energy.
segments.translation: 我认为如果你看看能源议程，没有能源我们就无法赢得人工智能竞赛。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And we made huge progress on energy.
segments.translation: 我们在能源方面取得了巨大进展。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: I'm hoping we're going to get permitting reform, which would be the biggest economic lever we could possibly get done over the next six months or the next 2 1/2 years.
segments.translation: 我希望我们能获得许可改革，这将是我们在未来六个月或未来两年半内可能实现的最大经济杠杆。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: We've closed the border.
segments.translation: 我们已经关闭了边境。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: We've stopped the flow of fentanyl.
segments.translation: 我们已经阻止了芬太尼的流入。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: We had 4000 people who died in Pennsylvania in the last year, The Biden administration at 1600.
segments.translation: 去年宾夕法尼亚州有4000人死亡，拜登政府时期有1600人。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: This year, it's down 60%.
segments.translation: 今年下降了60%。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Those same statistics nationally.
segments.translation: 全国范围内的统计数据也是如此。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And then there's huge intractable problems like the debt and the deficit, which are existential that we're not dealing with.
segments.translation: 然后还有巨大的、棘手的问题，比如债务和赤字，这些都是我们没有处理的生存问题。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And that's not a product so much of the filibuster, not the filibuster, that's a product of the polarization of our country and both sides taking advantage of anybody willing to to to look at a problem in a, in a hard.
segments.translation: 这与其说是阻挠议事的结果，不如说是我们国家两极分化的结果，双方都利用任何愿意认真看待问题的人。

segments.text: It's a huge problem.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And I don't, I don't think I listened carefully last night.

segments.text: I mean, I just want to tell you that is a huge, huge problem.
segments.translation: 我的意思是，我只想告诉你，这是一个巨大的、巨大的问题。

segments.text: That's growing.

segments.text: That median income in Pennsylvania is $52,000 a year.
segments.translation: 宾夕法尼亚州的中位数收入是每年52,000美元。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: When you guys say AI or AII mean these, these folks, they've been down this road once before when a bunch of smart rich people said we got the answer.
segments.translation: 当你们说人工智能或人工智能时，我的意思是，这些人以前也经历过一次，当时一群聪明的富人说我们有答案。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: It's called globalization.
segments.translation: 它叫做全球化。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And what happened in my hometown is there was a male of 2000 people that got gutted.

segments.text: It's now 100 people.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: So there is enormous anxiety, but it's because there's no path to getting ahead.
segments.translation: 所以存在巨大的焦虑，但这是因为没有前进的道路。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And everybody in this room, the last 10 years has been the greatest 10 years in the history of humanity for those who have assets.
segments.translation: 而这个房间里的每个人，过去十年对于那些拥有资产的人来说，是人类历史上最伟大的十年。

segments.speaker: Speaker 5
segments.text: So do you have a plan?
segments.translation: 那么你有什么计划吗？

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Yeah, well, there's, there's got to be, there's got to be a number of plans.
segments.translation: 是的，嗯，必须有，必须有许多计划。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Well, do you have a plan?
segments.translation: 那么你有什么计划吗？

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Because it's not just going to be me, it's going to be us.
segments.translation: 因为不仅仅是我，而是我们。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Because right now I'm listen, I'm AI am a beneficiary of, of capitalism.
segments.translation: 因为现在我听着，我是资本主义的受益者。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: I have been wildly fortunate because of capitalism, but we are we are going to lose capitalism unless we find a combination of a ways to address it.
segments.translation: 我因为资本主义而非常幸运，但除非我们找到一种结合的方式来解决它，否则我们将失去资本主义。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: So what are the ways the Invest America accounts is a perfect way right where you are building opportunity for the next generation.
segments.translation: 那么，投资美国账户是完美的方式，对吧？你正在为下一代创造机会。

segments.text: The the school choice provision in the Working Families Tax Cut Act $1700.

segments.text: Everybody in this room can give $1700 every year, billions of dollars that are going to go into a school choice for, for making sure everybody has equality of opportunity.
segments.translation: 这个房间里的每个人每年可以捐赠1700美元，数十亿美元将用于择校，以确保每个人都有平等的机会。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: If you don't do that at maximum scale and this moment leaves the majority of Americans behind, we're not going to be able to get anything.
segments.translation: 如果你不以最大规模做到这一点，而此刻却让大多数美国人掉队，我们将一事无成。

segments.speaker: Speaker 5
segments.text: Done.
segments.translation: 完成。

segments.speaker: Speaker 5
segments.text: Spend more money on programs.
segments.translation: 在项目上花更多的钱。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Yes, spend more money, but not not spend more, but spend more money in giving people opportunity.
segments.translation: 是的，花更多的钱，但不是花更多，而是花更多的钱来给人们机会。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: So the reason those two accounts are great, it takes it out of the government, circumvents the government.
segments.translation: 所以这两个账户之所以很棒，是因为它将钱从政府手中拿走，绕过了政府。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: It's based on incentives and a choice by people that have wealth.
segments.translation: 它基于激励和有钱人的选择。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: It's it's sort of Andrew Carnegie brought to present day.
segments.translation: 这有点像安德鲁·卡内基的现代版。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Take that wealth, put it in the hands of those who will benefit from it.
segments.translation: 把财富拿出来，交给那些能从中受益的人。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: But it's your choice.
segments.translation: 但这是你的选择。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: It's not dictated by the government.
segments.translation: 这不是政府规定的。

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: I think that's going to have to be part of the answer.
segments.translation: 我认为那将是答案的一部分。

segments.speaker: Speaker 6
segments.text: Does anyone in Congress subscribe to the notion that I think is rooted in, you know, empiricism, that the more we spend, the harder it is for people to have economic mobility?
segments.translation: 国会中是否有人认同这样一种观念，我认为这种观念植根于经验主义，即我们花得越多，人们实现经济流动的难度就越大？

segments.speaker: Speaker 6
segments.text: You know, and I think that there's a, a simplified notion that government has to play a role in driving people's progress.
segments.translation: 你知道，我认为有一种简化的观念，认为政府必须在推动人们进步方面发挥作用。

segments.speaker: Speaker 6
segments.text: And the truth is the more government intervenes in markets, the more inefficient and the more expensive those markets get.
segments.translation: 而事实是，政府对市场的干预越多，这些市场就越低效，成本就越高。

segments.speaker: Speaker 6
segments.text: And therefore the more inaccessible wealth and value creation is for any individual.
segments.translation: 因此，财富和价值创造对任何个人来说都越难以获得。

segments.speaker: Speaker 6
segments.text: And the freer the market, the less the government intervenes, the less the government is spending, the less the government is buying, the better things get for people.
segments.translation: 市场越自由，政府干预越少，政府支出越少，政府购买越少，人们的生活就越好。

segments.speaker: Speaker 6
segments.text: Generally speaking.
segments.translation: 一般来说。

segments.speaker: Speaker 6
segments.text: This is, and it seems to me every time I visit DCI Leave profoundly unhappy because I meet with people in Congress, and this is a notion that seems to be diametrically opposed to their viewpoints, that everything is about doing more for people.
segments.translation: 这是，在我看来，每次我去华盛顿特区，我都会非常不高兴，因为我遇到国会议员，而这种观念似乎与他们的观点截然相反，他们认为一切都是为了为人民做更多的事情。

segments.speaker: Speaker 6
segments.text: Government needs to do more on both sides of the aisle versus if the government did less, things would get more affordable, things would get more accessible, and people would have greater economic mobility.
segments.translation: 政府需要在两党之间做更多的事情，而不是如果政府做得更少，事情会变得更实惠，更容易获得，人们会有更大的经济流动性。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Well, I mean, you know, talk about the, the, the government now, we had not just one, we had two shutdowns.
segments.translation: 嗯，我的意思是，你知道，谈到政府，我们不仅有一次，我们有两次停摆。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Both were historic in terms of their length.
segments.translation: 两次停摆的持续时间都具有历史意义。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: You know, we couldn't just agree on very basic things and now we've shut the government down collectively for over 120 days or whatever now.
segments.translation: 你知道，我们甚至无法就非常基本的事情达成一致，现在我们已经集体关闭政府超过120天了，或者说现在是这样。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: So then that's one of the thing.
segments.translation: 所以这就是其中一件事。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: As a Democrat, I refuse to engage in that thing.
segments.translation: 作为一名民主党人，我拒绝参与那件事。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: If that's a core responsibility as a senator, keep our government open and for the love of God, find a way to agree enough to keep things open and put things in risk and make our country less, less safe.
segments.translation: 如果那是参议员的核心职责，保持我们的政府开放，看在上帝的份上，找到一种方法达成足够的共识，以保持事情开放，而不是让事情处于危险之中，让我们的国家变得不那么安全。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: You know, I'm proud to be a capitalist and our capitalism is the the one system that has proven to raise life's standard of humans across the globe.
segments.translation: 你知道，我很自豪成为一名资本家，而我们的资本主义是唯一被证明能够提高全球人类生活水平的制度。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: You know that.
segments.translation: 你知道的。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: And now people in my party and now, now we're having bad ID's refused to die.
segments.translation: 现在我党内的人，现在，现在我们有一些糟糕的观念，它们拒绝消亡。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: And now we're talking about socialism and and communists right now we have we have candidates now that I'm, I am a communist, these things.
segments.translation: 现在我们正在谈论社会主义和共产主义，现在我们有候选人，我，我是一个共产主义者，这些东西。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: And that's like, that seems interesting.
segments.translation: 这听起来很有趣。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: You know, what's your point now?
segments.translation: 你知道，你现在想说什么？

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Talk to anyone that's had to live under those kinds of regime.
segments.translation: 去和那些在这种政权下生活过的人谈谈。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Now they're all absolute capitalists right now.
segments.translation: 现在他们都是绝对的资本主义者。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: And that's that's absolutely the fact that the market will has fixed a lot of these kinds of problems.
segments.translation: 这绝对是事实，市场已经解决了许多这类问题。

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: You know, and I'm not terrified by AI.
segments.translation: 你知道，我并不害怕人工智能。

segments.text: Am I concerned about it 100% right now and with now mythos and other concerns about mass packing and a weaponizing it that way, now that's coming.
segments.translation: 我现在是否百分之百地担心它？是的，现在有了神话和其他关于大规模包装和武器化它的担忧，这些都来了。

segments.text: And now I think that should belong to America.
